name: Veramendi
title: Veramendi Homes & Neighborhood Guide | New Braunfels, TX
description: Compare Veramendi homes in New Braunfels: new construction, resale options, amenities, schools, and the property costs to check before buying.
answer: Veramendi is a master-planned New Braunfels community with new-home and resale options, trails, parks, and The Ledge amenity center. Compare the exact home’s total monthly cost, builder terms, school assignment, and phase of development before deciding.
intro: Start with the lot and the numbers, then compare the floor plans. Two homes advertised in Veramendi can have different builders, included features, closing dates, and ownership costs. A move-in-ready builder home and an owner-occupied resale also involve different negotiations. This guide helps you organize that comparison before a model-home visit.
facts: Compare builder inventory with resale listings
The Ledge pool and splash pad
New Braunfels ISD; verify by address
sections: Compare Veramendi new homes and resales
Builder inventory versus a resale

Ask for a written list of what is included in the specific builder home. Compare its lot premium, appliances, landscaping, window coverings, and closing terms with a resale that may already have those items. An advertised incentive is only useful once you compare the financing conditions and total price.
Lot position and construction activity

Walk the lot rather than relying on the model. Check backyard orientation, slope, drainage, nearby roads, and the location of future construction on the community plan. Visit at a different time of day to judge light, noise, and the route you will actually drive.
Amenities: separate what is open from what is planned
The Ledge and everyday outdoor access

The developer identifies The Ledge, a pool and splash-pad amenity center, alongside parks and trails. Ask which facilities your ownership includes, what access rules apply, and which routes connect your particular section. A feature on the master plan should not be assumed to be open.
The Outlook is a separate future project

The developer’s March 2026 announcement described The Outlook as a planned second amenity center. Confirm its present construction status and delivery schedule directly rather than treating a projected date as a guarantee.
Build a property-specific monthly budget
Taxes, districts, insurance, and association costs

Request the exact parcel’s current tax information, applicable special-district disclosures, association documents, and insurance quotes. A new home’s prior land-only tax bill can understate the cost after improvements are assessed. Compare the full monthly payment, not just the mortgage principal and interest.
School assignment and daily routes

The developer identifies Veramendi and Lamar elementary campuses within the community. Confirm the assigned campuses for the exact address and school year with NBISD. Test routes to work, shopping, and school at the times you would use them; a citywide drive-time estimate is not a commute plan.
faqs: Can I compare builder homes with Veramendi resale listings?

Yes. Compare both using the same budget and move-in deadline, including included features, financing terms, inspection findings, and estimated ongoing costs. Builder incentives and individual resale terms can change.
Does every Veramendi home have the same tax bill?
Do not assume so. Use the exact parcel and applicable taxing entities, check exemptions separately, and ask how a newly completed home will be assessed.
Are all announced amenities already open?
No. Distinguish existing facilities from planned projects. Ask the developer and association for the current status and access rules.

name: Mayfair
title: Mayfair Homes & Neighborhood Guide | New Braunfels, TX
description: Explore Mayfair homes in New Braunfels. Compare builders, quick move-ins, Fairway Park, planned Midtown development, schools, and purchase costs.
answer: Mayfair is a growing New Braunfels community with new homes, Fairway Park, and a developing Midtown district. Compare homes by builder, lot, included features, completion timing, and full ownership cost; verify future amenities and school assignments directly.
intro: Mayfair is a place to compare what you can use today with what is still being built. Its developer describes a community organized around homes, parks, trails, and a growing Midtown district. For a buyer, the important question is how the particular home and phase fit your move date, daily routes, and budget—not just the finished master-plan illustration.
facts: Multiple builders and quick move-in options
sections: Compare Mayfair builders on the same basis
Price the actual home, not the model

Request an itemized price for the lot, structural options, finish selections, and included equipment. Ask whether the model’s ceiling height, outdoor space, cabinets, and flooring are standard for the plan you are considering. Two similarly sized floor plans may produce very different final prices.
Match the home to your move date

A completed inventory home, a home under construction, and a to-be-built home have different timing risks. Ask for the present stage, the contractual completion terms, and what happens if your lease or PCS arrival precedes closing. Confirm registration and representation requirements before the first builder visit.
Understand parks and the Midtown buildout
Fairway Park and trails

The developer identifies Fairway Park as open, with a playscape, pump track, and disc golf. Check the route from a specific home to the park and the current trail connections. Distinguish public recreation areas from resident-only amenities and review the relevant access rules.
Midtown is developing in phases

Mayfair describes Midtown as a district for shopping, dining, work, and gathering spaces that is taking shape. Confirm which destinations are actually open and which are proposed or under construction. A future shop or amenity should not be the only reason a home fits your daily routine.
Check schools, costs, and daily travel
Verify the school year as well as the address

Mayfair identifies Comal ISD and an on-site elementary campus. Its school page also describes future school development. Use Comal ISD’s current attendance information to confirm assignments for the exact address and enrollment year; an on-site campus is not a guarantee of assignment.
Compare the recurring costs

Ask for the exact property’s tax and special-assessment disclosures, association charges, insurance estimate, and utility information. Compare a lender incentive with an alternative written loan estimate, including costs after a temporary buydown expires. Drive your work and shopping routes during normal travel times before committing.
faqs: Are Mayfair homes move-in ready?
Some builder offerings may be quick move-ins, while others are under construction or to be built. Availability changes; confirm the status and written closing terms of the specific home.
Is Midtown Mayfair complete?
The developer describes Midtown as developing. Verify the opening status of individual shops, services, and amenities rather than relying on the eventual master plan.
How should I compare builder incentives?
Get the conditions in writing and compare total purchase price, lender fees, rate terms, closing costs, and the payment after any temporary discount ends.

name: Vintage Oaks
title: Vintage Oaks Homes & Homesites | New Braunfels Guide
description: Compare Vintage Oaks homes and homesites near New Braunfels. Understand custom-building decisions, lot conditions, amenities, restrictions, and ownership costs.
answer: Vintage Oaks offers custom homes and homesites in the New Braunfels Hill Country, with pools, trails, fitness facilities, and other community amenities. Compare a completed home with the complete cost and timeline of building on a particular lot.
intro: A homesite and a finished home are two different purchases. In Vintage Oaks, the right comparison includes what the land can accommodate, the cost of preparing it, the community’s building requirements, and the amount of time you want to spend on a custom project. Start there before deciding which view or floor plan to pursue.
facts: Topography, buildable area, and service connections
Pools, lazy river, trails, fitness, and sport courts
Buy a finished home or investigate a custom build
sections: Buying a completed home versus building
Evaluate the finished home as its own property

Review the home’s age, maintenance, inspections, design choices, and any transferable warranties. Compare the lot and usable outdoor space as carefully as the living area. Existing landscaping, fencing, and outdoor improvements can affect your overall budget when comparing it with a new build.
Make the lot-plus-build budget complete

Ask a builder to evaluate the specific site before relying on a construction estimate. Discuss clearing, grading, drainage, foundation design, driveway, utilities, wastewater arrangements, and landscaping. The land price and a floor-plan quote alone are not a complete project budget.
Read the lot and the restrictions
Slope and orientation change the project

Walk the usable building area and discuss access, setbacks, easements, trees, sun exposure, and drainage with appropriate professionals. A broad acreage number does not tell you the size or shape of the area where a house and outdoor improvements can be placed.
Confirm the rules for your section

The developer describes both gated and non-gated neighborhoods and build-when-ready options. Obtain the current restrictions and architectural requirements for the actual lot. Confirm approval steps, builder qualifications, construction timing rules, and any additional section-specific charges before purchasing.
Amenities and everyday ownership
Check access as well as the amenity list

The official community site lists pools, a lazy river, trails, a fitness club, and sport courts. Ask about ownership eligibility, access procedures, operating hours, reservation policies, and any separate fees. Tour the facilities you expect to use rather than assuming every section has the same walking route.
Compare the ongoing costs and routes

Request current association documents and the property’s tax, insurance, utility, and maintenance information. For a larger lot, budget for exterior upkeep as well as the home itself. Confirm school assignments directly with the district and test your own routes to work and services.
faqs: Should I buy land before choosing a builder?
It helps to have a qualified builder evaluate the specific lot before you commit. Site conditions, restrictions, utilities, and design requirements can materially change feasibility and total cost.
Is every Vintage Oaks section gated?
The official community site describes both gated and non-gated neighborhoods. Verify the section and any access or fee requirements for the specific property.
Can I use my own builder?
The developer advertises builder-choice options. Confirm the current architectural rules and builder requirements for the actual homesite before relying on that option.

name: River Chase
title: River Chase Homes & Neighborhood Guide | New Braunfels
description: Explore River Chase near New Braunfels: custom homes, the private river park, utilities by section, property restrictions, and questions to ask before buying.
answer: River Chase is a custom-home community along FM 306 between New Braunfels and Canyon Lake. Its association describes a private Guadalupe River park and a clubhouse recreation area. Utilities and lot conditions vary by section, so compare the exact property rather than assuming all homes have the same services.
intro: River Chase deserves a property-by-property search. A home’s section affects the utility questions to ask, and private community river access is different from owning riverfront land. Compare the house, lot, services, association requirements, and your daily routes as one package.
facts: FM 306 corridor between New Braunfels and Canyon Lake
sections: Understand the two sides of the community
Verify water and wastewater arrangements

The POA distinguishes western Units 1–3 from eastern Units 4–10. It describes well water in the western portion and water lines in the eastern portion, with aerobic septic systems in both. Verify the actual service providers, equipment, permits, maintenance history, and any inspection needs for the specific home.
Inspect the usable lot

Compare driveway access, slope, drainage, easements, vegetation, and the location of existing improvements. If you are considering a pool, workshop, or future addition, confirm restrictions and site feasibility before assuming the acreage will accommodate it.
Private river access is not a waterfront promise
The association’s river park

The POA identifies a private river park on the Guadalupe, plus a separate clubhouse recreation area with pools, courts, trails, and a pond. Confirm ownership eligibility, access cards, guest rules, reservation requirements, and any closures directly with the association.
Investigate water-related conditions separately

A neighborhood river amenity does not establish whether an individual parcel is waterfront or outside a flood hazard area. Review the particular property’s disclosures, available flood information, drainage, and insurance options with appropriate professionals. Water levels and access conditions can change.
Plan for ownership beyond closing
Restrictions and maintenance responsibilities

Obtain the current deed restrictions, architectural rules, association resale information, dues, and any outstanding compliance issues. For a home with private water or wastewater equipment, include service, testing, and replacement needs in the ownership budget.
Schools, travel, and recurring costs

The POA identifies Comal ISD; confirm campus assignments for the address and school year directly with the district. Drive the FM 306 route at the times you travel and compare the property’s taxes, insurance, utilities, and upkeep alongside its asking price.
faqs: Does owning in River Chase mean my house is riverfront?
No. The association’s private river park is a community amenity. Verify whether the individual property has any frontage or separate access rights.
Do all River Chase homes have the same utilities?
No. The POA describes different water arrangements between portions of the community. Confirm actual services, equipment, and maintenance requirements for the exact property.
Can I build a workshop or add a pool?
That requires review of the particular lot, easements, wastewater layout, deed restrictions, and architectural approval process. Confirm feasibility before buying for a planned improvement.
